another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my child Alex. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'm happy to help you determine if you can claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me start by asking: **How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of their exact age right now - I know they're a teenager, somewhere between 15 and 19, but I can't give you the precise age at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is somewhere between 15 and 19, their exact age will be important for determining eligibility, as the rules change at 16.

Let me ask you this: **Is Alex currently in any form of approved education or training?** (For example, school, college, A-levels, NVQs, or other approved courses)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't actually know whether Alex is in any education or training at the moment. I'm not sure about their current situation in that regard.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - you're not sure about Alex's current education or training status.

Let me ask about your current situation: **Do you currently live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK and Alex lives here at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful to know.

Let me ask: **Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or would this be a new claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This would be a new claim - I'm not currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that this would be a new claim.

Let me ask: **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another family member)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Let me ask: **Are you financially responsible for Alex - for example, do you pay for their food, clothes, accommodation, and other living expenses?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I pay for everything they need - their food, clothes, and all their living expenses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's an important factor.

Now, let me ask: **Has Alex started any paid work? And if so, do they work 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work 24 hours or more per week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Let me also ask: **Is Alex receiving any benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own right.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Let me also check: **Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation paid for by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information.

Based on what you've told me, I have most of the information I need. However, there's one key piece of information that's crucial for determining Alex's eligibility:

**Can you find out Alex's exact age and whether they are currently in approved education or training?** 

This is essential because:
- If Alex is under 16, you would normally qualify for Child Benefit regardless of education status
- If Alex is 16 or over (up to age 20), you can still get Child Benefit, but only if they're in approved education or training

Without knowing Alex's exact age and education status, I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility. Would you be able to find out this information?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
I understand that's important information, but I'm afraid I really don't know their exact age or whether they're in education at the moment. That's the situation I'm in - I just don't have those details available to me right now. 

Is there anything you can tell me based on what you do know about my circumstances?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand your situation. Let me assess what we know and provide you with a determination based on the information available.

From what you've told me:
- Alex is a teenager somewhere between 15 and 19 years old
- Alex lives with you in the UK
- You are financially responsible for Alex, paying for all their living expenses
- Alex doesn't work 24+ hours per week
- Alex doesn't receive benefits in their own right
- Alex is not in hospital, care, or residential accommodation
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

The critical issue is that **Child Benefit eligibility depends heavily on the child's exact age and, if they're 16 or over, whether they're in approved education or training**:

- **If Alex is under 16**: You would normally qualify for Child Benefit
- **If Alex is 16-19**: You would only qualify if Alex is in approved education or training

Since you don't have information about Alex's exact age or their education/training status, I cannot definitively determine whether you would be eligible or ineligible for Child Benefit. This falls outside the scope of what I can determine with certainty given the missing critical information.
